Hi Chiara,

I'm actually not sure! It really depends on if FragPipe outputs the same files/formats that DIAUmpire provides. You are correct that we need those three files. You can actually see examples of those files included in MSstats (see the code below). If FragPipe uses DIAUmpire but outputs the data differently these will not work.

On a side note, I know they also use DIA-NN and we do have a converter for DIA-NN so you could potentially use that as well.

Devon

```
library(MSstats)

diau_frag = system.file("tinytest/raw_data/DIAUmpire/dia_frag.csv",
                             package = "MSstatsConvert")
diau_pept = system.file("tinytest/raw_data/DIAUmpire/dia_pept.csv",
                             package = "MSstatsConvert")
diau_prot = system.file("tinytest/raw_data/DIAUmpire/dia_prot.csv",
                             package = "MSstatsConvert")
annot = system.file("tinytest/annotations/annot_diau.csv",
                    package = "MSstats")
diau_frag = data.table::fread(diau_frag)
diau_pept = data.table::fread(diau_pept)
diau_prot = data.table::fread(diau_prot)
annot = data.table::fread(annot)
diau_frag = diau_frag[, lapply(.SD, function(x) if (is.integer(x)) as.numeric(x) else x)]
# In case numeric columns are not interpreted correctly

diau_imported = DIAUmpiretoMSstatsFormat(diau_frag, diau_pept, diau_prot,
                                         annot, use_log_file = FALSE)
head(diau_imported)
```

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

We observed extreme log2 fold changes in control vs treatment contrasts. Tracking this down, it seems this is due to missing value imputation.

Please see image below, showing PSMs input to MSstatsTMT as well as MSstatsTMT feature output with imputed values:

While it's clear to me that a small number e.g. 2.8e-42 will result in -138 in log2 space. What I'm questioning is if this is a reasonable value and assumption for TMT abundances.
Shouldn't there be a minimum value e.g. 1 in log2 space for imputed values? This would be in order for extreme log2 ratios (numerator vs denominator condition) can't happen.

We're using Proteome Discoverer PSMs files of TMT16plex as input, and processed using MSstatsTMT version 2.8.0.

Thank you for all your efforts!!

Best,
David

messages.subject: Troubleshooting FragPipe input to dataProcess
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
Thanks for putting out and maintaining a package so well. I am extremely new to MSstats so forgive the naive question. I have searched previous issues and while they are somewhat similar I couldnt find one with this specific issue. If I missed something please just point me towards it if you could!

I have, hopefully, a fairly simple problem with FragPipe output being fed to dataProcess. This was from an exploratory label-free DDA experiment. Experimental setup is
No bio or tech reps per condition
3 fractions per condition
Lots of different conditions, lots of missing values due to tissue source differences
Here is screenshot of the input data (slightly modified from initial FragPipe output due to issue listed below):

So with the MSstats.csv in hand, I do the following:
Take output from FragPipe and run it through FragPipetoMSstatsFormat()
Complains there might be fractions (there are) or tech reps (there are NOT)
"** MSstats suspects that there are fractionations and potentially technical replicates too. Please add Fraction column to the input."
Add Fraction column with fraction numbers (as seen in screeenshot)
Finishes FragPipetoMSstatsFormat() BUT with lots of "Warning: no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf" messages - possibly due to NAs?
Feed output to dataProcess() and  get following error:
"Error in merge.data.table(input[, colnames(input) != "newABUNDANCE", with = FALSE], : Elements listed in `by` must be valid column names in x and y" Which seems to suggest it is trying to generate a df without matching columns.
Here is traceback:

However, if I change all fraction numbers to 1 (not correct, as these were fractions) it seems to assume files are tech reps and dataProcess() will finish generating the dataProcess() object/list.

I've tried several other things such as making the file smaller to test if it's a memory issue (doesn't seem to be). I've also confirmed the test DDA set included with MSstats runs normally. It seems clear it may be an issue with feature metadata formatting for this dataset but I am scratching my head as to why, when including the correct fraction number causes it to error out. Maybe MSstats is expecting more replicates or I am missing a setting change? But the test DDA dataset is fairly simple and doesn't have any replicates so I suppose it should be ok. Any insight is appreciated!

Cheers
Carlos

messages.subject: Re: FragPipe-DIA-NN-MSstats question about annotation file
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

Thanks to a lot of help from Alison Chaves, we came up with this workaround. I was unable to fix the original error by simply modifying the annotation file and instead also had to modify the DIA-NN output. It seems like this is caused by some syntax changes in the column headings of the DIANN output obtained from FragPipe. For reference, I'm running dplyr_1.1.3 diann_1.0.1 MSstats_4.10.0 BiocManager_1.30.22 MSstatsConvert_1.11.5.

diann_report <- diann_load("diann-output.tsv") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Run = sub("2022-02-09-KB-SY79-", "", Run)) %>%
    group_by(Stripped.Sequence,
              Modified.Sequence,
              Q.Value,
              Lib.Q.Value,
              Lib.PG.Q.Value,
               Protein.Group,
               Precursor.Charge,
               Fragment.Quant.Raw,
               Run,
               Genes.MaxLFQ) %>%
      summarize() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Condition = str_extract(Run, "dilution|DIA"),
                BioReplicate = str_extract(Run, "DMSO|DMSO|DMSO"),
                FragmentIon = NA,
                ProductCharge = NA,
                IsotopeLabelType = "L") %>%
         rename(StrippedSequence = Stripped.Sequence,
                ModifiedSequence = Modified.Sequence,
                ProteinNames = Protein.Group,
                QValue = Q.Value,
                LibQValue = Lib.Q.Value,
                LibPGQValue = Lib.PG.Q.Value,
                FragmentQuantCorrected = Fragment.Quant.Raw,
                PrecursorCharge = Precursor.Charge,
                Intensity = Genes.MaxLFQ)

annotation_file2 <- diann_report %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    dplyr::select(Run, BioReplicate, Condition) %>%
    distinct()
    ```
This seems to work as a temporary workaround, but i wanted to share with you all in case others encounter this issue.

Best,

Keri
